raw_response:
I will keep to the crop pattern I know best: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. In Quzhou County, that is the safest way for me to make grain and protect my income. I am 64, so I do not want a crop that needs too much fine management or too much market risk. Wheat and maize fit my experience, the local weather, the local water conditions, and the machines and inputs I can get nearby. I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize because I want stable yield, not trouble. I will fertilize, but not push too hard, because fertilizer is expensive and too much can waste money and damage the crop. I will irrigate wheat more than maize because wheat in our area often needs water in key stages, while summer maize can use the rainy season better. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier and cheaper for me than deep ploughing every season. I will spray only when needed, mainly for weeds, aphids, rust, and corn borers, because I want to control costs and avoid unnecessary pesticide use. My goal is steady harvest, manageable work, and lower risk.
